title: MIŽIGÁROVÁ v. SLOVAKIA
summary: In the case of Mižigárová v. Slovakia, the applicant, Mrs. Miluša Mižigárová, a Slovak national of Roma origin, brought a complaint against Slovakia following the death of her husband, Mr. Ľubomír Šarišský, in police custody. The case highlighted the acute vulnerability of Roma and Travellers to police violence and the lack of effective investigations into such incidents, reflecting broader patterns of discrimination and mistrust between Roma communities and law enforcement. On the evening of 12 August 1999, Mr. Šarišský, then 21 and in good health, was arrested in Poprad on suspicion of bicycle theft. During his interrogation at the police station, he was taken to a separate office by an off-duty officer, handcuffed to a radiator, and later shot in the abdomen with the officer’s service pistol. Despite being hospitalized, Mr. Šarišský died four days later from his injuries. Conflicting accounts emerged regarding the circumstances of the shooting and the presence of physical injuries, with the applicant reporting visible bruises and swelling on her husband’s body. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Articles 2 (right to life), 3 (prohibition of inhuman or degrading treatment), 13 (right to an effective remedy), and 14 (prohibition of discrimination). The Court found the application admissible and scrutinized the adequacy of the investigation into Mr. Šarišský’s death. This case is significant as it underscores the persistent risks faced by Roma and Travellers in police custody and the urgent need for independent, thorough investigations into allegations of police violence, set against a historical backdrop of systemic abuse and impunity in Slovakia and across Europe.
